title: Effective syntax for order-invariant first-order queries
area: Database theory and finite model theory
formal: Editorial effective-syntax variant: for every finite relational vocabulary tau, is there a decidable set S_tau of finite sentence codes, a total computable evaluator E_tau, and a total computable compiler C_tau into order-invariant first-order sentences, satisfying the soundness and expressive-completeness requirements below, uniformly in tau?
definitions:
An order-invariant FO sentence phi over tau∪{<} has the same truth value on (A,<1) and (A,<2) for every finite nonempty tau-structure A and every two linear orders on its domain. It therefore defines a Boolean isomorphism-invariant query on unordered structures. Equality is logical; tau contains finitely many relation symbols of specified finite arity and no designated order. Structures are encoded by a finite domain [n] and explicit relation tables.

The selected syntax S_tau is a decidable collection of finite binary strings. E_tau(s,A) must be a total computable Boolean function on well-formed s and finite A. C_tau(s) must effectively return an FO(tau∪{<}) sentence which is order-invariant on all finite structures, with E_tau(s,A) equal to its truth value under every order. Completeness requires that every order-invariant FO(tau∪{<}) sentence has some s∈S_tau defining the same query on every finite A. No effective inverse map from an arbitrary order-invariant formula to s is required. Uniformity in tau means one collection of algorithms accepts a finite vocabulary description as an extra argument.

This compiler requirement is an explicit editorial strengthening of the broad phrase effective syntax. Merely listing all FO sentences and semantically promising that they are invariant does not give a decidable syntax. Merely evaluating a sentence under all orders also does not ensure that the resulting query is expressible by order-invariant FO.
answer_criterion: Prove in Lean existence of such decidable syntax, evaluator and compiler, with soundness and completeness on all finite structures, or prove that they cannot exist. Undecidability of testing invariance for arbitrary FO sentences alone does not rule out a different effective syntax with the same expressive power.
context: Schweikardt’s tutorial distinguishes order-invariant expressibility from syntactically decidable logics and states undecidability of checking invariance. The present question asks for a separate effective presentation.
why: An effective syntax would make semantic order invariance available as a usable formal language.

progress.text: The tutorial develops order-invariant FO and explains why its direct semantic syntax is not decidable.

import_provenance.original_title: An effective syntax for order-invariant first-order queries
import_provenance.original_statement: Is there an effectively presented logic defining exactly the queries expressible by first-order formulas with an auxiliary linear order whose choice does not affect the result? This is an editorial continuation of Gurevich’s work showing that order-invariant first-order logic can express more than ordinary first-order logic.

context_blocks.text: Schweikardt’s tutorial distinguishes order-invariant expressibility from syntactically decidable logics and states undecidability of checking invariance. The present question asks for a separate effective presentation.

sentences: Order-invariant FO may inspect an auxiliary order but its answer cannot depend on that order.
The target is an effective syntax describing exactly those finite-structure queries.
The selected variant requires a computable compiler to invariant FO and a total evaluator.
It does not require deciding invariance of arbitrary given formulas.
This compiler requirement is explicitly marked as an editorial choice.
